pr_title: Make H2 WebSockets ignore MaxRequestBodySize and MinRequestBodyDataRate
pr_body:
Contributes to #42101 (I didn't do the part yet about preventing use of the request or response body for these types of requests).
Fixes #42224

H2 WebSockets were using the normal H2 request body, meaning they were subject to the MaxRequestBodySize and MinRequestBodyDataRate limits. This caused issues like an idle blazor page to disconnect every 6 seconds.

I've also further distinguished the CONNECT scenario from the Upgrade scenario by giving it its own state bools.

### Describe the bug

**When binding the https for "Kestrel" via appsettings.json, --urls or set the ASPNETCORE_URLS environment variable, Blazor server app site can be launched with https://*:5001, but it will be disconnected about every 5s.**

**Application Name** : eShopOnBlazor, OqtaneFramework, EasyDataBasicDemoBlazorAppServerNet5, Blazorise,BlazorPolyfill(Blazor Server apps running on .net7 preview 6)
**OS:** Windows 10 RS5
**CPU**: X64
**.NET Build Number:** dotnet-sdk-7.0.100-preview.6.22313.7
**Also can check details from Devdiv Bug:**   https://devdiv.visualstudio.com/DevDiv/_workitems/edit/1555938

2) Add this line to appsettings.json for workaround : (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/42161)
```
{
  "Kestrel": {
    "Endpoints": {
      "Http": {
        "Url": "http://localhost:5000"
      },
      "Https": {
        "Url": "https://localhost:5001"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

3) Publish the app
4) Run the app
5) Go to https://localhost:5001

review_comments: @halter73 this is what you recommended, but it's actually stricter than Upgrade which only prevents modification after upgrade is called. Neither null out the size limit field, they just ignore it. The data rate limit property is similarly ignored rather than cleared.
I think this is good. With extended CONNECT requests, middleware has not chance to run before the "upgrade" so-to-speak. The request is pre-upgraded.
Talked offline: yes, basically the context gets reset separately and will have the correct value when the Http2MessageBody is reset
Isn't it always false here though? Let's not make it any more convoluted than necessary.
Could make `ExtendedConnect` virtual, and override in `Http2MessageBody` to wrap `Context.IsExtendedConnectRequest`. Simpler, safer, but very small perf hit of virtual property call.
IsExtendedConnectRequest is initialized before Http2MessageBody is reset.
Let's do the same thing in `TryStop`.
